profile.beat: AI memory and connectivity, mega-cap technology, precious metals and macro positioning.
profile.style: High-conviction fundamental and technical commentary tied to a research subscription. Uses personal holding claims, earnings comparisons, proprietary indicators and options positioning to argue for multi-month upside.
profile.cadence: Frequent originals and replies, recurring earnings summaries and promotional references to a paid research service.
profile.revisits: Micron remains a repeatedly defended largest holding in 2097530037645750366; Astera and Credo receive fresh thesis updates in 2100656388213260795 and 2100659845158355245.
profile.caveats: Short incremental window rather than two months. Holdings, performance and valuation claims are self-reported; underlying paid research and chart images are unavailable. The pre-FOMC expectation of no rate change is contradicted by the subsequent hike reported in the same bundle. DRAM, GOLD and SILVER are used as thematic or commodity labels and are not assigned to an equity instrument.

narrative: The account argues that memory scarcity is becoming the dominant driver of AI-industry economics. Micron remains the strongest explicit personal commitment, while Astera and Credo are presented as increasingly attractive beneficiaries of connectivity demand. The author expects mega-cap technology to emerge from prolonged consolidation despite macro anxiety. Ahead of FOMC the author expects a hold, then reports a hike while retaining the bullish broader-market view. AI safety and slower frontier release pacing are interpreted as compatible with rising compute and memory requirements. By the end of the window, the author sharpens the upside case for Astera, Credo and Nvidia and continues a separate bullish metals thesis.

picks.prospect: Memory scarcity supports continued leadership and rerating.
picks.thesis: The author identifies Micron as the largest holding and sees a durable demand imbalance alongside strong leadership.

For weeks I’ve been saying CXMT is only going to make the memory shortage worse as CXMT is simply eating up more supply despite actually being a threat to the demand of the three juggernauts 

The idea that memory has remotely gotten close to peaking couldn’t be any more wrong by many analysts on here in the past couple weeks 

$MU $SKHY $KOSPI $DRAM

I broke down ALL MAJOR EARNINGS from this quarter so far into one cheatsheet:

Save this image 🙂

-- The verdict? --

Tech is RAPIDLY shifting its focus towards who has the best exposure in the ongoing memory pandemic.

We have gone from who had the best AI exposure from 2024-2026 to whoever has the best memory exposure from 2026-2028.

These are not my words, this is the common denominator which appeared in all the major earnings from the management teams themselves.

The market will be forced to re-rate memory, compute, and connectivity higher as the memory pandemic is only getting worse.

The biggest beneficiaries of the memory crisis?

Micron - $MU
Nvidia - $NVDA
Astera Labs - $ALAB
Credo - $CRDO
Marvell - $MRVL
Sandisk - $SNDK
Western Digital - $WDC

It is an understatement to say memory is doing something right now which we genuinely will not see repeated in many decades to come

I will continue to ignore any noise about this industry like I have been since making Micron $MU my largest holding to date last year around $100 a share

Invest into memory's byproducts now, or be left behind

I might have bias towards Sanjay because he literally changed my life through Micron, as well as many people I know, 

but much of my conviction in Micron since last year was due to his organic leadership traits. 

He pioneered an industry which had odds completely against it, and he continues to still portray the same cool calm collected traits which instills a magnitude of confidence into those who look into his work.

When people say a “CEO DRIVEN COMPANY,” Sanjay is literally at the forefront of that statement 

$MU

sources.quote:
It may sound crazy, but I believe $META is actually not too far out from being in the same basket as these cybersecurity and cloud observability names 🤫

The backbone of META and this industry ultimately rely on one major advantage that traditional software no longer has https://t.co/fvTm0q9OWJ

User database is about to become one of the biggest assets in tech moving forward imo. That's one edge that AI cannot replicate, no matter how good a frontier model is. 

That's what makes cloud observability and cybersecurity names so great in this era of tech. It's being able to combine AI with user database that only a handful of companies have which they collected throughout the traditional software run. Now they get to use that info to its finest capabilities
